b.backbone: Take the explicit periodic Steinberg group St_12(R) over a finitely presented matrix-nil graded algebra; phases of long words and homological stability let degree truncations detect all elements.
b.quote: We construct an infinite group with an ordinary finite presentation in which every element has finite order, answering the finitely presented Burnside question negatively.

a.backbone: A recursive Hilbert-ball colouring of dyadic partitions turns approximate invariance of a finite set into an approximate fixed point of an explicit positive-displacement map, giving a uniform Følner-defect bound.
a.quote: The proof turns approximate translation invariance of finite averages of scalar functions on \(F\) into an approximate fixed point of a Lipschitz map on a Hilbert ball.

b.backbone: A recursive Hilbert-ball colouring of dyadic partitions turns small Folner boundary into an approximate fixed point of an explicit positive-displacement Lipschitz map, yielding a uniform boundary lower bound.
b.quote: The proof turns approximate translation invariance of finite averages of scalar functions on \(F\) into an approximate fixed point of a Lipschitz map on a Hilbert ball.

a.backbone: Uniform bounded-height theorem for self-quasi-isometries (volume-growth comparisons, compactness limits) turns the quasi-action into a homomorphism whose kernel has polynomial growth; Gromov and finiteness properties give polycyclicity.
a.quote: Transporting the left translation action of $H$ across a quasi-isometry gives maps of $G$ with uniform quasi-isometry bounds that respect multiplication up to a uniformly bounded error.

b.backbone: Prove uniform bounded height for self-quasi-isometries of solvable Lie groups via random charts and limiting affinity; the height action leaves a polynomial-growth kernel, giving virtual polycyclicity.
b.quote: We construct a submersive scheme for each limiting normalized group. Its persistence under nearby group laws will then give uniform generation by compactness.

a.backbone: A kernel relation yields a planar surface of word disks; a multi-block fixed-space theorem (cohomological intersection) plus spectral-phase subadditivity forces every boundary word, hence the coefficient, trivial.
a.quote: The proof estimates one unitary operator in two ways. Mixing disks of the same type gives an upper bound for its phase. Reading the operator around the boundary gives an exact phase formula.

b.backbone: A kernel element yields a planar disk-and-band surface; a multi-block unitary fixed-space theorem and spectral-phase subadditivity show one nontrivial boundary word is impossible, so the coefficient is trivial.
b.quote: The upper bound forces the extra term to vanish, so this word is trivial.

a.backbone: Sample a random nested-table presentation: with probability tending to one it is aspherical with linear filling, and any geometric CAT(0) action yields a limiting configuration forcing an impossible flat square.
a.quote: The proof is an existence argument and does not give an effective size for $K$.

b.backbone: A random nested-table presentation is aspherical with linear filling with high probability; a hypothetical CAT(0) action yields, via energy minimization and tangent cones, a configuration contradicted by flat-square rigidity.
b.quote: The proof is an existence argument and does not give an effective size for $K$.

a.backbone: Explicit amalgam of a free group with a direct product: height extensions have cost near one; a Bernoulli-to-rank transfer and deterministic rank bound keep Bernoulli cost above one.
a.quote: We construct a finitely generated group with two essentially free probability-measure-preserving actions of different costs.

b.backbone: Construct an amalgam of F_100 with a direct product; height extensions have cost near one, while compression, Bernoulli transfer and a planar rank bound keep Bernoulli cost above one.
b.quote: We construct a finitely generated group with two essentially free probability-measure-preserving actions of different costs.

a.backbone: Gap gives an initial subvolume box exponent; replica norm comparisons scanning collars improve it repeatedly; ordered tile families and the entropy chain rule then give the area law.

b.backbone: Bound collar mutual information via spectral-gap norm comparisons on replica operators (bootstrapping a box exponent), then entropy chain rules over ordered region families give the area law.
b.quote: If each region shares little information with the complement of $A$ together with the earlier regions of its own family, two applications of the entropy chain rule cancel all individual region entropies.

a.backbone: Deterministic reduction from a QMA-complete lattice Heisenberg problem: place unit nuclei realizing tuned wells, derive Hubbard/Heisenberg effective model by perturbation bounds, and exclude lower-energy continuum states.
a.quote: A deterministic classical polynomial-time reduction produces polynomially many nuclei at distinct rational positions and polynomially many electrons, with polynomial rational bit lengths and threshold separation at least one.

b.backbone: Explicit poly-time reduction from a QMA-complete lattice spin Hamiltonian to unit-charge nuclear configurations, via Hubbard effective models, localized modes, and continuum many-electron energy estimates.
b.quote: A deterministic classical polynomial-time reduction produces polynomially many nuclei at distinct rational positions and polynomially many electrons, with polynomial rational bit lengths and threshold separation at least one.

a.backbone: Energy bounds from C2-cofiniteness give strong locality; annulus estimates integrate unitary modules; fusion positivity and a permutation-orbifold argument unitarize all modules; cited comparison theorems give the tensor equivalence.
a.quote: The central ordering issue is that a positive form on $V$ does not initially give positive forms on its modules or fusion products. We first work with modules already carrying such forms.

b.backbone: Sequential chain: energy bounds give strong locality and a net; annulus estimates integrate modules; fusion positivity and permutation orbifolds unitarize all modules; the CWX functor gives the braided equivalence.
b.quote: This supplies a starting point for the following sequence.

a.backbone: Construct total functions with Forrelation-certified column certificates and outward pointers; a quantum tournament search gives the upper bound and a planted-input direct-product argument gives the randomized lower bound.
a.quote: We construct a total function whose accepting certificate belongs to one column.

b.backbone: Construct a total function from Forrelation instances with addressed certificates and pointers; quantum tournament search gives the upper bound, a planted-input direct-product argument gives the randomized lower bound.
b.quote: We construct a total function whose accepting certificate belongs to one column.

a.backbone: Build a group from Osajda-labelled expanders as graphical relators, construct a local operator with uniform spectral gap whose kernel projection has irrational trace; Lück's rational-trace theorem blocks surjectivity.
a.quote: Thus a projection in \(C_r^*(G)\) with irrational trace would obstruct surjectivity. We construct such a projection.

b.backbone: Build a torsion-free group from a graphical small-cancellation tower whose permutation tables are chosen by a probability law ensuring expansion; Bott classes and small-trace projections witness Baum-Connes failure.
b.quote: There is a probability law on all the permutation tables such that every auxiliary incidence has centered singular norm at most the fixed number $\rho<1$

a.backbone: Finite factors: uniform commutator amplification plus amenable-cocycle averaging give a near-identity isomorphism; then infinite factors via modular alignment and crossed products, then centers; small unitaries implement these isomorphisms.
a.quote: Transporting this isomorphism back and applying the commutator estimate gives a small unitary on the original Hilbert space.

b.backbone: Prove finite-factor conjugacy (commutator amplification plus boundary averaging), reduce infinite factors via modular alignment and crossed products, then assemble through centers and arbitrary Hilbert spaces.
b.quote: \Cref{fig:proof} displays how the finite-factor result enters both the finite and infinite cases and how they meet in the final reductions.

a.backbone: Existing criteria reduce to a core fixed-point equality; the multiplication identity R=L·exp(iX⊗Y), obtained from the absolute bicentralizer theorem and repeated tensor tests (each by contradiction), yields the commutation.
a.quote: Existing bicentralizer criteria reduce our task to showing that the extension of $\gamma$ to $B\rtimes_{\sigma^\varphi}\R$ has fixed algebra $N'\cap c(M)$.

b.backbone: Assume failure (self-bicentralizing counterexample); left/right multiplication isometries satisfy R=L exp(iX tensor Y), and uniform modular-energy estimates with repeated tensor tests contradict; pass to the core for general inclusions.
b.quote: Suppose that the theorem fails, and choose $(M,\varphi)$ as in \eqref{eq:self}.

a.backbone: Verify equivariant uniform property Gamma for Szabó–Wouters absorption by building commuting orbit rows in the central sequence algebra, Gaussian quadratics over Følner sets, a weighted Haar unitary and equal-trace projections.
a.quote: If the action has equivariant uniform property Gamma, it is cocycle conjugate to its tensor product with the trivial action on \(\Zalg\).

b.backbone: Build commuting orbit rows in the central sequence algebra; a joint CLT and Gaussian quadratics over Følner sets give an invariant Haar unitary (equivariant Gamma); apply Szabó-Wouters.
b.quote: Finally, weighting traces by elements of \(A\) yields a central invariant unitary with Haar distribution relative to \(A\).

a.backbone: Without characters, a finite tensor power carries a matrix-cone homomorphism with full corner from representation-independent tensor labels; a stable-rank-free Rørdam–Winter criterion upgrades it to a dimension-drop map, embedding Z centrally.

b.backbone: Construct a unital homomorphism from the dimension-drop algebra into a finite tensor power via a matrix-cone map with full corner, then embed into central sequences to obtain Z-absorption.
b.quote: For any separable subalgebra $E\subset F_\omega(A)$, we construct a unital map from $D$ into $F_\omega(A)\cap E'$.

a.backbone: Reduce to a faithful central state; on the normalizer part build a random Bernoulli coloring via mixed determinantal polynomials and iterative pinning; elsewhere use random diagonal unitaries.
a.quote: We construct a measurable coloring there that has uniform conditional color marginals and makes the pinched matrix small on any prescribed finite-radius ball with arbitrarily high probability.

b.backbone: Reduce to a faithful central state; pave the normalizer part by a mixed-determinantal-polynomial measurable coloring on a Bernoulli extension and the complement by atomless-kernel random labelling.
b.quote: We separate the algebra generated by normalizers from its orthogonal complement with respect to a state-preserving expectation.

a.backbone: Graph measurements of orthogonal copies reduce failure to finitely many explicit equalities, excluded by a four-entry contradiction under proper infiniteness; cutoffs and iteration give arbitrary-entry diagonalization, hence strong pure infiniteness.

b.backbone: A graph of orthogonal copies reduces failure of mixed-entry diagonalization to finitely many equalities, excluded by ultraproduct contradictions; ideal cutoffs then give a global support estimate.
b.quote: A graph of orthogonal copies first turns possible failure into finitely many explicit equalities. Once those equalities have been excluded, ideal cutoffs convert the resulting nonvanishing into one global support estimate.

a.quote: Let $G$ be a minimal-order counterexample to \eqref{eq:HQC} for $p=2$.

b.backbone: A minimal-order counterexample has a Lie-type component in a short list; for each family, frame cycles, dimension estimates and propagation produce nonzero rational homology, a contradiction.
b.quote: Let $G$ be a minimal-order counterexample to \eqref{eq:HQC} for $p=2$.

a.backbone: Prove finiteness of continuous stabilizer cohomology for a broad coefficient class via p-adic geometry (Fargues–Fontaine towers, Kummer supports, Laurent models) with uniform vanishing; descent then gives degreewise finite generation.

b.backbone: Reduce to finiteness of continuous stabilizer cohomology with mod-p coefficients, proved by downward induction over height strata using Fargues-Fontaine tower geometry and a highest-degree contradiction.

a.backbone: Construct a detecting map from L_K(3)S to a K(2)-local spectrum preserving a nonzero rational degree -3 stabilizer class; any splitting equivalence would kill it on pi_-3, a contradiction.
a.quote: Any equivalence \(X\simeq\mathcal W_3\) would force its lower horizontal map to vanish on \(\pi_{-3}\), and hence force the same for \(\tau_T\). This contradicts \cref{thm:main}.

b.backbone: Construct an explicit ordered fracture filtration of the height-three overlap, identify its attachments via cohomology of completed Lubin-Tate strata, and show one is nonzero, refuting strong splitting.
b.quote: For every prime \(p\geq5\), we construct an explicit eight-stage filtration of \(L_2L_{K(3)}\mathbb S_p^\wedge\) by the local-sphere layers in the height-three chromatic-splitting pattern.

a.backbone: Plus construction on an explicit five-generator presentation gives a D(2) complex with a torsion character of vanishing twisted H_2; a cyclic-cover tower obstruction shows no 2-complex has such a character.
a.quote: We construct a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex satisfying the $D(2)$ finiteness condition but not homotopy equivalent to any finite CW complex of dimension at most two.

b.backbone: Construct an explicit presentation with zero twisted H_2 for a character detecting an order-two element, apply a finite plus construction; a cyclic-tower obstruction excludes any finite 2-complex model.
b.quote: Section~\ref{sec:construction} then gives a five-generator, four-relator presentation and a perfect normal subgroup generated normally by two powers.

a.backbone: Conformally reduce to scalar curvature -1; build a bounded-cohomology detector, iterate sweeps to entropy metrics, prove a measured degree estimate, and compare dual chains to bound simplicial volume.
a.quote: The work of this paper is the passage from that qualitative vanishing result to a uniform quantitative estimate.

b.backbone: Conformally reduce to scalar curvature -1; via a bounded-cohomology detector, iterated graph deformations to entropy metrics, and a measured degree estimate, compare simplicial volume to volume.
b.quote: The work of this paper is the passage from that qualitative vanishing result to a uniform quantitative estimate.

a.backbone: Construct a global Kahler-Ricci flow, prove Harnack inequalities via a disc envelope, obtain contracting holomorphic charts, and iterate polynomial models so inverse charts converge to a biholomorphism onto C^n.

a.backbone: Assume finitely many prime geodesic images; bound temporary sublevel classes by a uniform filling estimate via string-topology cut-join, then double-loop symmetry and equivariant classes give a contradiction.
a.quote: We first control these temporary classes and then use the symmetry of double loops to obtain a contradiction.

b.backbone: Assume finitely many prime geodesic images; uniform filling via string-topology cut-join identities and resonance controls transient homology classes, and double-loop symmetry yields a contradiction.
b.quote: Assume that a metric on $S^n$, $n\ge3$, has only finitely many prime geodesic images.

a.backbone: Assume bounded scalar curvature with a singularity; bubble-tree scale selection plus a static Einstein–Hilbert tree inequality force root Ricci energy to vanish, contradicting the prescribed change of the outermost scale.

b.quote: Section~\ref{sec:contradiction} applies the static theorem separately to arbitrary sequences of active time patches.

a.backbone: Prove a localized Łojasiewicz-type gradient inequality for Gaussian area near the shrinker via a finite-jet obstruction, then propagate it with a bootstrap to finite length and unique convergence.
a.quote: Gradient inequalities connect small stationary defect to finite length of the rescaled flow.

b.backbone: Using Bamler-Kleiner tangent structure, a finite-jet obstruction yields a localized Lojasiewicz-type gradient inequality; iterative graph improvement and propagation with summable motion force convergence of rescalings.

a.backbone: Cone-like metric whose sphere link follows a periodic path of equal-area metrics; eigenline exchanges at double eigenvalues cycle a spectral band, giving many harmonic functions with average rate below k.
a.quote: We construct a periodic path $H(s)$ of sphere metrics near the round metric, all with the same pointwise area form.

b.backbone: Construct a warped metric on R^3 whose sphere links follow a periodic path cycling eigenlines through crossings, so selected harmonic modes average rates below k, exceeding the Euclidean count.
b.quote: We construct a periodic path $H(s)$ of sphere metrics near the round metric, all with the same pointwise area form.

a.backbone: Layered exact finite expansion of interacting histories over time cells, centered against the Boltzmann solution; history integrals and tree counting with a single energy budget bound remainders, summed to convergence.
a.quote: Their layered expansion retains the earlier histories of correlated remainders while extracting the factors approximated by the kinetic solution.

b.backbone: Layered cluster expansion over time cells with centering at layer cuts; chronological induction controls remainders through tree counting and dynamical-cutoff estimates, giving L1 convergence of marginals.
b.quote: We induct on $j$ in chronological order, with $R_k$ already controlling both remainder types whenever $k<j$.

a.backbone: Multiscale block-renormalization of effective densities with a shooting choice of terminal coupling yields convergent Schwinger functions, then OS axioms, non-Gaussianity and mass gap.
a.quote: The organization by successive block integrations belongs to the renormalization-group tradition of Kadanoff and Wilson~\cite{Kadanoff,Wilson}.

b.backbone: Renormalization group: iterate block integrations with a step theorem controlling effective densities, shoot to a terminal coupling, and pass to the continuum limit verifying OS axioms and mass gap.
b.quote: The organization by successive block integrations belongs to the renormalization-group tradition of Kadanoff and Wilson~\cite{Kadanoff,Wilson}.

a.quote: Our first geometric estimate bounds the number of times the double-dimer loops can cross a slab of fixed positive width. We prove it in a finite Temperleyan rectangle.

b.backbone: Transfer-matrix particle estimates bound slab crossings, giving tightness of loop curves; subsequential limits are identified with nested CLE4 via cited puncture convergence and exclusion of invisible paths.

a.backbone: Spin/percolation cuts give circuit and moment bounds; reflection positivity with a spectral sum rule fixes the covariance, boundary comparison removes boundary effects, and Wick recursion identifies subsequential limits as GFF.
a.quote: The proof combines reflection positivity, a spectral sum rule, and boundary comparison with Gaussian moment identities.

b.backbone: Tightness plus identification of every subsequential limit: reflection positivity, pin motion and boundary comparison yield harmonic moment identities and a Wick recursion, which determine the Gaussian free field.
b.quote: The main task is to identify every subsequential limit $H$ of the integer height field.

a.backbone: Joint tightness from circuit and comparison estimates; reflection positivity plus screening identifies the height as GFF; recursive stopped two-valued local sets of that field then identify every subsequential cluster limit.
a.quote: Our proof first obtains joint tightness, then identifies every subsequential limit as the canonical construction of \cref{thm:main}.

b.backbone: Prove joint tightness, identify the height limit as a GFF via reflection positivity, screening and Wick moments, then identify current clusters as canonical two-valued local sets, characterizing every subsequential limit.
